newsitem.title: USA: Clergyman who used Minnesota escort service quits.
newsitem.headline: Clergyman who used Minnesota escort service quits.

text.p: The Rev. A.C. Stein has resigned his administrative post with the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America after admitting he patronised a Minneapolis escort service, the church said on Friday.

Stein, submitting his resignation as director of human resources, told leaders of the Chicago-based church he twice procured companions from the "Black Tie Escort Service," which provided women, while on business trips in 1994.
He said nothing sexual happened during the trysts and that he received "therapeutic massages." He used a church-issued credit card on which he paid the bills himself.

His credit slip, along with those of about 1,000 other clients, showed up on a list acquired by media outlets in Minneapolis after the escort service's owner was given a one-year jail sentence for soliciting prostitution.
Stein, 50, left his post, from which he had hired the church headquarters' 400-person staff, on Wednesday.

"Pastor Stein has made many contributions to the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America in his 10 years of church-wide service. (We) are saddened to have to share this difficult news," the Rev. Robert Bacher, the church's executive for administration, said in statement to members.
The church has about 5.2 million members in the United States.
